lessons.claim: ★ In Buckingham pi's i = n - r, the r is 'the rank of the dimensional matrix' and not the number of base dimensions. A counter-example was measured -- the variables (v, gdot, L) have 3 base dimensions (M,L,t) but M appears in no variable, so the rank is 2, i=1, and that dimensionless number is gdot*L/v. Counting by 'the 3 base dimensions' gives i=0 and misjudges that there is no dimensionless number. ★ A BD dimensionless system is overdamped so the mass often disappears, which puts it in exactly this situation
